title: xⁿ on [0, 1]: the area shrinks to 0
caption: As n grows, xⁿ hugs the x-axis except right at x = 1, and the area under it is 1/(n + 1): 1/2, 1/3, 1/6, 1/21, … → 0, matching the limit of the integrals found by dominated convergence.
alt: Four curves on [0, 1]: y = x, x squared, x to the 5 and x to the 20, each lower and closer to the axis than the last, all meeting at the point (1, 1).
description: Every curve xⁿ lies between 0 and the constant function 1 (the dominating function).
For 0 ≤ x < 1, xⁿ → 0; only at the single point x = 1 does it stay at 1.
The areas are 1/(n + 1): 1/2 for n = 1, 1/3 for n = 2, 1/6 for n = 5, 1/21 for n = 20, shrinking to 0.

checks.name: the area under x^1 on [0, 1] is 1/2
the area under x^2 on [0, 1] is 1/3
the area under x^5 on [0, 1] is 1/6
the area under x^20 on [0, 1] is 1/21
